sentences.text:
Versus
 1. The State of Bihar
 2. Manisha Devi wife of Jitendra Kumar Pandit, D/o- Dilip Thakur Village-
 Dallu Tola Ward no-19, Ps- Forbesganj Dist- Araria
 ... ... Opposite Party/s

=
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Pankaj Kumar Jha, Adv.
 For the State : Mr. Rajesh Kumar, App
 For the O.P. No. 2 : Mr. Santosh Kumar Verma, Adv.
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Harish Kumar
 Oral Order
3 13-12-2023

Heard Mr. Pankaj Kumar Jha, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner and Mr.
Santosh Kumar Verma, learned counsel for the O.P. No. 2.
Learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State is also present.

2. The petitioner, who happens to be husband of the O.P. No. 2, apprehends his arrest in connection with Mahila P.S. Case No. 46 of 2022, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 341,
323, 307, 420, 498A, 504, 506/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. Allegedly, the marriage of the petitioner was solemnized with O.P. No. 2 on 26.05.2015 as per the Hindu customs and rites.

However, after leading peaceful happy life Patna High Court CR. MISC.
No.57265 of 2023(3) dt.13-12-2023 for some days, she was subjected to torture on account of non fulfillment of dowry.
It is further stated that a panchaiti was also held and an agreement was executed allowing both the parties to live separately.
In the meantime, the couple also blessed with one son and one daughter.
Lastly, the O.P. No. 2 has been ousted from her matrimonial home on 25.07.2022 resulting into lodging of the present FIR.

sentences.text:
While drawing the attention of this Court to the agreement entered into between the parties,
submission has been made on behalf of the petitioner that admittedly both the parties are signatory to the agreement and on this premise the petitioner has also filed a divorce case bearing Matrimonial Case No. 125(M) of 2022, which is pending before the Principal Judge, Family Court,
Araria.
It is the further submission of the petitioner that as soon as the O.P. No. 2 received notice in the divorce case, she filed the present FIR.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the O.P. No. 2 submits that apart from the allegation and counter allegation this is the fact that the marriage was solemnised in the year 2015 and couple have also been blessed with two children and the O.P. No. 2 still wanted to live with the petitioner accepting the fact that the petitioner is suffering from disability.

Patna High Court CR. MISC.
No.57265 of 2023(3) dt.13-12-2023 6.

Considering the fair stand of the learned counsel for the parties, this Court deems it fit and proper to relegate the matter to the Mediation Centre, Patna High Court for exploring the chance of amicable settlement between the parties.
7. In view thereof, both the parties are, hereby, directed to appear on 17.01.2024 before the Patna High Court Mediation Centre along with a copy of this order.

On receipt thereof, after affording proper opportunity of hearing to them, efforts shall be made by the learned Mediator for a mutually acceptable settlement between the parties and a report thereafter be submitted to this Court by the Patna High Court Mediation Centre before the next date of hearing.

8. Re-notify this matter on 07.02.2024 along with the report of the learned Mediator.
9.
The interim protection granted to the petitioner under order dated 20.09.2023 shall continue.

(Harish Kumar, J) Anjani/-
